C3: The excess distance billed is $9.45 (6.70 km × $1.4101/km, the trip's own distance fare ÷ distance km), and on a metered RydeTAXI fare that amount is refundable to the extent the extra kilometres are not exempt under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5. [F5 F7] [RD-2 FARE-1]

claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter ($46.12 total, base $3.90 + distance $31.84 for 22.58 km + time $8.91), so every extra kilometre driven enters the fare; the trip ran 22.6 km against an optimal 15.9 km, i.e. +6.7 km (+42%).

The GPS record shows two off-route segments, and each is an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route: segment 21:42–21:49 added 2.69 km (4.26 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.57 km) and segment 22:02–22:09 added 3.13 km (4.57 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.43 km).

The excess distance billed is $9.45 (6.70 km × $1.4101/km, the trip's own distance fare ÷ distance km), and on a metered RydeTAXI fare that amount is refundable to the extent the extra kilometres are not exempt under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

The driver's written statement that lanes were blocked by an accident 'so I went round it' is a post-trip claim, and the only accident record in the file is a single event reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE after Sheares Avenue Exit, which is earlier than the 21:42 and 22:02 off-route segments but is corroboration for at most the road it names, not for two separate loops reaching 1084 m and 997 m away from the optimal route.

The chat record contains no in-app messages at all between rider and driver, so there is no rider message before either segment that could amount to consent, and the driver's statement of a verbal explanation after the fact does not constitute consent.

No stop, request or message by the rider preceded either segment: the file records no rider-originated stopping request, and the only 'stop'-like content is the driver's own post-trip explanation, so the extra kilometres on both segments are unexempt.

The driver's 90-day profile shows 1 dispute upheld, but 0 of those were route disputes, so the repeated-route-deviation threshold in RD-6 is not met and no account flag is requested; the profile facts are offered only in support of the refund request, not as the basis of the route finding.

weaknesses: The driver will rely on F12 (accident reported 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route) together with F10/F11 (PIE band 5, KPLX band 4 over 21:26–22:17) to argue reasonable cause under RD-4 and, if the judge accepts it for the whole corridor, both segments become exempt and the refund is $0.

The single F12 event is only tied to one named expressway and to one report time; neither the GPS facts F3/F4 nor any other record in the file names the actual roads driven during the 21:42–21:49 and 22:02–22:09 segments, so on the driver's best reading the judge could treat the road actually taken as undetermined rather than clearly off-route (G13), which would send the case to a human rather than produce an award.

The rider's own history (F14) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld, which the driver may use to argue this complaint is unfounded, and my side has no message evidence at all (F8) to show the rider ever objected during the trip.

claims.assertion: The trip is RydeTAXI and metered (F7), so the only money capable of being refunded is the extra distance billed, which the fare record quantifies as $9.45 for 6.70 km (F5).
There are two off-route segments on the record: 21:42–21:49 adding 2.69 km (F3) and 22:02–22:09 adding 3.13 km (F4); together 5.82 km (F3, F4).

The driver's own statement says an accident blocked the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway and the detour was unavoidable (F9), but that statement alone cannot justify anything because a statement is not a system record.

That statement is independently corroborated for the first segment: an LTA DataMall accident was reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE, 0 m from the optimal route (F12), i.e. inside the 300 m matching band and reported before the 21:42 segment began.

The second detour interval 22:02–22:09 (F4) also falls inside the same recorded incident window, which was still listed from 21:26 through 22:17, and the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway was still only at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) throughout (F11, F12).
No chat record exists between rider and driver (F8), so the rider's assertion that she 'never agreed to any change' is undisputed and the driver does not claim any rider consent.
The driver has no prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (F15), so the repeated-offender condition for an account referral is not met on the record.
The billed excess (F5) exceeds the sum of the two off-route segments (F3, F4) by 0.88 km, which is the untraceable remainder the policy leaves out of any refund calculation.

weaknesses: Segment 22:02–22:09 (F4) starts 34 minutes after the accident was reported (F12) and the driver's statement (F9) does not say which detour it explains; the estimator may find the second loop unexplained and refund its 3.13 km, i.e. $4.41 of the $9.45 in F5.

The total actual distance of 22.6 km against 15.9 km optimal (F1) and duration 34.2 min against 21.4 min (F2) show the meter ran 42% long, which reads badly even if each segment has a cause; the rider will rely on F1 and F2.

The accident record (F12) says 'Avoid lane 2' — an instruction to avoid a lane, not the whole expressway — so the rider will argue the optimal route was still passable and the driver was not entitled to leave it entirely.
The driver has 1 dispute and 1 upheld in 90 days (F15), which is enough for the rider to ask for an account referral even though the 90-day window shows no upheld route case.
The driver's explanation is a post-trip statement (F9) and not a contemporaneous message, so it carries less weight than the system records the rider will cite.

events.body:
→ D1 (concedes): Accepted: the fare record is a metered RydeTAXI total (F7) and the only recoverable head of loss is distance, quantified by the fare record at $9.45 for 6.70 km (F5); our dispute is over how much of that is exempt, not over the quantum basis. [F7 F5] [RD-2]

→ D3 (concedes): Accepted: a post-trip driver statement (F9) is not a system record and cannot by itself supply the 'reasonable cause' that RD-4 requires. [F9] [RD-4]
→ D4 (concedes): Conceded for the first segment only: the accident in F12 sits 0 m from the optimal route and was reported at 21:26, before the 21:42–21:49 segment in F3 began, so we do not press for the 2.69 km in F3. [F12 F3] [RD-4]
→ D5: Contested: RD-4(a) requires the incident to justify the substituted stretch of optimal route, yet F12 records one accident on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway with the instruction 'Avoid lane 2' — a lane instruction, not closure of the route — and the KPLX was still flowing at band 4 (30–39 km/h) (F11), so by 22:02, 36 minutes after the 21:26 report (F12), nothing in the record explains why the driver looped up to 997 m off the optimal route (F4); band evidence is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment by itself (RD-4(b)). [F12 F11 F4] [RD-4]
→ D6 (concedes): Accepted that no rider-originated consent exists: there are no in-app messages at all (F8), so no rider message precedes either segment and both segments remain unexempt from consent. [F8 F3 F4] [RD-5]
→ D7 (concedes): Accepted: the driver's 1 upheld 90-day dispute is not a route dispute (F15), so RD-6 is not met and we do not seek flag_account; the profile facts (F14, F15) are offered only as background and carry no weight in the route finding. [F15 F14] [RD-6]
→ D8 (concedes): Accepted in part: the 0.88 km difference between the billed excess (F5) and the two segments (F3, F4) is the untraceable remainder that RD-2 leaves out of the calculation, so our refund is computed only on the segment kilometres and does not touch it; note the point cuts the other way too, since it means the $9.45 in F5 is not itself proof of the segment distances. [F5 F3 F4] [RD-2]
→ C2: Our claim C2 stands as a statement of the record (F3, F4) but is qualified by the concession on the first segment: only the 21:42–21:49 segment (F3) is now pressed as unexempt. [F3 F4] [RD-1]
Revised ask: refund_partial $4.41

Accepted: a post-trip driver statement (F9) is not a system record and cannot by itself supply the 'reasonable cause' that RD-4 requires.

Conceded for the first segment only: the accident in F12 sits 0 m from the optimal route and was reported at 21:26, before the 21:42–21:49 segment in F3 began, so we do not press for the 2.69 km in F3.

claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter ($46.12 total, base $3.90 + distance $31.84 for 22.58 km + time $8.91), so every extra kilometre driven enters the fare; the trip ran 22.6 km against an optimal 15.9 km, i.e. +6.7 km (+42%).

The GPS record shows two off-route segments, and each is an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route: segment 21:42–21:49 added 2.69 km (4.26 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.57 km) and segment 22:02–22:09 added 3.13 km (4.57 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.43 km).

The excess distance billed is $9.45 (6.70 km × $1.4101/km, the trip's own distance fare ÷ distance km), and on a metered RydeTAXI fare that amount is refundable to the extent the extra kilometres are not exempt under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

The driver's written statement that lanes were blocked by an accident 'so I went round it' is a post-trip claim, and the only accident record in the file is a single event reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE after Sheares Avenue Exit, which is earlier than the 21:42 and 22:02 off-route segments but is corroboration for at most the road it names, not for two separate loops reaching 1084 m and 997 m away from the optimal route.

The chat record contains no in-app messages at all between rider and driver, so there is no rider message before either segment that could amount to consent, and the driver's statement of a verbal explanation after the fact does not constitute consent.

No stop, request or message by the rider preceded either segment: the file records no rider-originated stopping request, and the only 'stop'-like content is the driver's own post-trip explanation, so the extra kilometres on both segments are unexempt.

The driver's 90-day profile shows 1 dispute upheld, but 0 of those were route disputes, so the repeated-route-deviation threshold in RD-6 is not met and no account flag is requested; the profile facts are offered only in support of the refund request, not as the basis of the route finding.

weaknesses: The driver will rely on F12 (accident reported 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route) together with F10/F11 (PIE band 5, KPLX band 4 over 21:26–22:17) to argue reasonable cause under RD-4 and, if the judge accepts it for the whole corridor, both segments become exempt and the refund is $0.

The single F12 event is only tied to one named expressway and to one report time; neither the GPS facts F3/F4 nor any other record in the file names the actual roads driven during the 21:42–21:49 and 22:02–22:09 segments, so on the driver's best reading the judge could treat the road actually taken as undetermined rather than clearly off-route (G13), which would send the case to a human rather than produce an award.

The rider's own history (F14) shows 2 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld, which the driver may use to argue this complaint is unfounded, and my side has no message evidence at all (F8) to show the rider ever objected during the trip.

claims.assertion: The trip is RydeTAXI and metered (F7), so the only money capable of being refunded is the extra distance billed, which the fare record quantifies as $9.45 for 6.70 km (F5).
There are two off-route segments on the record: 21:42–21:49 adding 2.69 km (F3) and 22:02–22:09 adding 3.13 km (F4); together 5.82 km (F3, F4).

The driver's own statement says an accident blocked the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway and the detour was unavoidable (F9), but that statement alone cannot justify anything because a statement is not a system record.

That statement is independently corroborated for the first segment: an LTA DataMall accident was reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway towards TPE, 0 m from the optimal route (F12), i.e. inside the 300 m matching band and reported before the 21:42 segment began.

The second detour interval 22:02–22:09 (F4) also falls inside the same recorded incident window, which was still listed from 21:26 through 22:17, and the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway was still only at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) throughout (F11, F12).
No chat record exists between rider and driver (F8), so the rider's assertion that she 'never agreed to any change' is undisputed and the driver does not claim any rider consent.
The driver has no prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days (F15), so the repeated-offender condition for an account referral is not met on the record.
The billed excess (F5) exceeds the sum of the two off-route segments (F3, F4) by 0.88 km, which is the untraceable remainder the policy leaves out of any refund calculation.

weaknesses: Segment 22:02–22:09 (F4) starts 34 minutes after the accident was reported (F12) and the driver's statement (F9) does not say which detour it explains; the estimator may find the second loop unexplained and refund its 3.13 km, i.e. $4.41 of the $9.45 in F5.

The total actual distance of 22.6 km against 15.9 km optimal (F1) and duration 34.2 min against 21.4 min (F2) show the meter ran 42% long, which reads badly even if each segment has a cause; the rider will rely on F1 and F2.

The accident record (F12) says 'Avoid lane 2' — an instruction to avoid a lane, not the whole expressway — so the rider will argue the optimal route was still passable and the driver was not entitled to leave it entirely.
The driver has 1 dispute and 1 upheld in 90 days (F15), which is enough for the rider to ask for an account referral even though the 90-day window shows no upheld route case.
The driver's explanation is a post-trip statement (F9) and not a contemporaneous message, so it carries less weight than the system records the rider will cite.

points.response: Accepted: the fare record is a metered RydeTAXI total (F7) and the only recoverable head of loss is distance, quantified by the fare record at $9.45 for 6.70 km (F5); our dispute is over how much of that is exempt, not over the quantum basis.
Accepted: the record shows two off-route segments, 2.69 km (F3) and 3.13 km (F4), totalling 5.82 km, and each is reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.
Accepted: a post-trip driver statement (F9) is not a system record and cannot by itself supply the 'reasonable cause' that RD-4 requires.

Conceded for the first segment only: the accident in F12 sits 0 m from the optimal route and was reported at 21:26, before the 21:42–21:49 segment in F3 began, so we do not press for the 2.69 km in F3.

Contested: RD-4(a) requires the incident to justify the substituted stretch of optimal route, yet F12 records one accident on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway with the instruction 'Avoid lane 2' — a lane instruction, not closure of the route — and the KPLX was still flowing at band 4 (30–39 km/h) (F11), so by 22:02, 36 minutes after the 21:26 report (F12), nothing in the record explains why the driver looped up to 997 m off the optimal route (F4); band evidence is corroboration only and cannot exempt a segment by itself (RD-4(b)).
Accepted that no rider-originated consent exists: there are no in-app messages at all (F8), so no rider message precedes either segment and both segments remain unexempt from consent.

Accepted: the driver's 1 upheld 90-day dispute is not a route dispute (F15), so RD-6 is not met and we do not seek flag_account; the profile facts (F14, F15) are offered only as background and carry no weight in the route finding.

Accepted in part: the 0.88 km difference between the billed excess (F5) and the two segments (F3, F4) is the untraceable remainder that RD-2 leaves out of the calculation, so our refund is computed only on the segment kilometres and does not touch it; note the point cuts the other way too, since it means the $9.45 in F5 is not itself proof of the segment distances.
Our claim C2 stands as a statement of the record (F3, F4) but is qualified by the concession on the first segment: only the 21:42–21:49 segment (F3) is now pressed as unexempt.
Conceded that the trip was metered RydeTAXI and that extra kilometres enter the fare (F7, F5); that is exactly why this case turns on RD-4 and not on any dispute about the billing mechanics.

The two segments exist as recorded (F3, F4), but calling them 'unexplained' ignores the one item of evidence RD-4 accepts: an LTA incident reported at 21:26 on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route (F12), inside the 300 m band and before the 21:42 segment began.

The refundable pot is at most the $9.45 billed excess (F5), but it is already overstated by the rider: their own request of $5.82 equals only the two segment figures of 2.69 km and 3.13 km (F3, F4), i.e. $8.21, which shows the claim is not even internally computed from F5 — no refund is owed once RD-4 exempts both segments.

The incident record is not limited to a single moment: it was reported 21:26 and remains listed in the window through 22:17, and the same expressway was still at speed band 4 (30–39 km/h) across 21:26–22:17 (F11, F12), which covers both the 21:42–21:49 and 22:02–22:09 segments (F3, F4) on the road being avoided.
Agreed that no consent exists (F8); the driver does not rely on any rider message or on any verbal claim, only on the RD-4 incident evidence (F9, F12).
Conceded — no rider-originated stop request appears in the file (F8); this was never a rider-requested stop but a traffic avoidance, which is why RD-4 and not RD-3 applies.
Neither side seeks an account flag and the driver's record shows 1 upheld dispute, 0 of them route-related (F15), so RD-6 is not engaged and no penalty should attach to a traffic-forced reroute.
